faqs.q: Which areas in Delhi are known for Korean food?
faqs.a: Majnu ka Tilla and Humayunpur near Safdarjung Enclave are known for small, casual Korean eateries and cafes, and Satya Niketan, Hauz Khas Village and Malviya Nagar also have Korean options. Gurgaon has several Korean restaurants too if you are willing to travel a little further.

faqs.q: Is Korean food in Delhi suitable for vegetarians?
faqs.a: Yes, many Korean restaurants and cafes offer vegetarian versions of popular dishes such as bibimbap, kimbap, japchae, tteokbokki and ramyeon. Traditional kimchi, broths and some sauces can contain fish sauce or seafood, so ask the staff if you want a strictly vegetarian meal.

faqs.q: What Korean dishes should a beginner try first?
faqs.a: Good dishes to start with are bibimbap, a mixed rice bowl with vegetables, kimbap rice rolls, japchae glass noodles and bulgogi, a marinated grilled meat, which are flavourful without being very spicy. If you enjoy heat, try tteokbokki or kimchi stew, and end with bingsu, a shaved-ice dessert.

faqs.q: Is eating Korean food in Delhi expensive?
faqs.a: It varies a lot. Small eateries in student and market areas serve noodles, kimbap and tteokbokki at modest prices, while Korean BBQ restaurants and mall outlets cost considerably more. Menus and prices change often, so check the current menu and opening hours before you go.
